item.description:

Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-24 Statistica medica, igiene generale e applicata e scienze infermieristiche generali, cliniche, pediatriche e ostetrico-ginecologiche e neonatali

The project aims to develop and apply spatial statistical methods to investigate the relationships between environmental and climatic exposures and the risk of acute and chronic diseases and, where possible, to estimate causal effects. The methodological framework will include geostatistical models, models for areal data and point process models. The analyses will focus on exposures to extreme temperatures and precipitation, drought, wildfire smoke and air pollutants (ozone, PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, NO₂ and NOₓ). Health outcomes will include cancer, cardiometabolic and respiratory diseases across the life course, as well as all-cause and cause-specific mortality.

The Early Stage Researcher will be actively involved in investigating the endothelial-modulating potential of extracellular vesicles derived from colorectal cancer specimens and cell lines (CRC-EVs), using both in vitro and in vivo approaches, as well as in assessing the effects of their pharmacological modulation. In particular, the researcher will investigate in vitro the effects of colchicine and its derivatives on the intracellular fate of CRC-EVs and on the molecular pathways underlying their biological activity. In addition, the researcher will conduct experiments in in vivo murine models to investigate CRC-EV biodistribution.
